$comment: Datasheet Schema v1.0. MIT. https://github.com/nkorai/datasheet-schema. This file is self-contained and validates with no external references.
title: Datasheet Schema
description: A machine-readable schema for electronic-component datasheet specifications. Each value records the test conditions under which it holds and a reference to its source in the datasheet. Existing standards omit both.

schemaVersion.description: The Datasheet Schema version this document conforms to.

pinout.description: Physical pins with normalized functions, so a tool can bind a pin by function rather than by vendor pin name.

parameters.description: All specified values. Absolute-maximum, recommended-operating, electrical, thermal, and ESD data are held here as parameters and distinguished by each measurement's limitClass rather than by separate tables. This allows one envelope to describe any component family.

notes.description: Free text for a reviewer, covering anything ambiguous, conflicting, or spread across variant tables.

family.description: Component family. Determines which parameter dictionary applies.

package.description: Package designator as printed, for example SOT-23-5.

polarity.description: The rail polarity of a regulator or reference, declared so a consumer never has to infer it from the sign of extracted values. positive is the default and MAY be omitted; negative marks a negative-rail part (a negative LDO or reference) whose output, input, and their conditions are negative numbers. When negative, min and max of a range keep numeric ordering (min is the more-negative bound), so an input range of -20 V to -2.3 V has min -20, max -2.3. bipolar is for a dual-rail or tracking part.

msl.description: Moisture sensitivity level, for example MSL1.

temperatureGrade.description: Qualification or temperature grade, for example -40..125 or AEC-Q100 Grade 1.

orderingVariants.description: The orderable variants covered by this datasheet.

outputVoltageV.description: Fixed output option, when this variant pins a voltage.

packing.description: Tape and reel, tube, or similar.

function.description: Normalized semantic function. A controlled vocabulary that families extend, in the same way the parameter key vocabulary is extended by a family dictionary. Recommended values: IN, OUT, GND, EN, NC, BYP, ADJ, FB, PG, SENSE, BIAS, PAD for regulators and references, and G, D, S for field-effect transistors. A validator MAY constrain the set per family. Uppercase, matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$.

parameter.title: Parameter
parameter.description: One canonically-keyed characteristic. A family dictionary, for example dictionary/ldo-1.0.json, defines the legal keys, their units, and vendor aliases. The schema keeps the parameter shape family-agnostic so every family reuses it.

key.description: Canonical parameter key from the family dictionary, for example dropout_voltage, psrr, reference_voltage, or thermal_resistance_junction_ambient.

group.description: Family-scoped functional group, for example regulation or protection.

aliases.description: Vendor synonyms for this parameter, for example ripple rejection for psrr. Normalizing naming in the schema rather than in downstream code keeps documents interoperable across manufacturers.

measurements.description: One entry per distinct condition set. A parameter specified across several load currents or frequencies, such as dropout, PSRR, or quiescent current, has one measurement per point.

measurement.title: Measurement
measurement.description: A value with its unit, the conditions under which it holds, the table it came from, and provenance.

limitClass.description: The kind of limit this value represents. absolute_max is a stress limit and operation beyond it may damage the device. recommended is the specified operating range. characterized is a measured or guaranteed electrical characteristic. A consumer must not treat an absolute_max value as an operating value.

conditions.description: The test conditions under which this value holds. An open list of typed axes so it generalizes across families. An LDO uses I_OUT and V_IN, a MOSFET uses V_GS and V_DS, a buck converter adds F_SW. The axes that govern the value should be present.

stimulus.description: For dynamic parameters such as load or line transient response and start-up, the applied step. Modeled here because the from, to, and slew fields recur for load steps, line steps, and switching edges.

conditionsVerbatim.description: The test conditions exactly as printed in the datasheet, retained alongside the parsed axes so nothing is lost in normalization.

sourcePage.description: 1-indexed datasheet page this value was read from.

sourceTable.description: The table it came from, for example Electrical Characteristics.

statistic.description: The statistical form of the value, when a parameter is specified in more than one, so that a peak-to-peak figure and an RMS figure of the same quantity (for example reference output noise) are machine-distinguishable rather than differing only in a verbatim string. rms, peak_to_peak, and peak are the usual noise forms; mean is occasionally used.

guarantee.description: The datasheet's basis for the value, from the specification footnotes. production_tested is 100% tested in production (usually the bold min/max limits). by_design and by_characterization are ensured but not production-tested. typical is a typical value that is not a guaranteed limit. This is the guarantee basis, distinct from limitClass (which kind of limit) and from review/confidence (extraction trust).

review.description: Extraction review state for this value, so a consumer can tell a machine-extracted number from a human-checked one. unchecked is raw extractor output; confirmed means a reviewer verified it against the page as-is; edited means a reviewer corrected it. Absent means not recorded. Advisory, like confidence: it is not the schema's verified flag.

confidence.description: Advisory extraction confidence for this specific value, 0 to 1. Per-measurement companion to document-level provenance.confidence. MUST NOT be read as verification; see review for the checked/unchecked state.

allOf.$comment: A characterized value must cite its page. Absolute-maximum stress rows may lack test conditions.

value.title: Value
value.description: IEC 61360 level roles. nom is a nominal or target value, for example a fixed 3.3 V option. typ is a typical measured value. At least one role is present.

conditionAxis.title: Condition axis
conditionAxis.description: One test-condition dimension. param uses a controlled vocabulary where possible, defined in the specification, but any string is allowed so family-specific axes extend it. Provide a scalar value, or a min and max range, or a note. A unit is required when a numeric value, min, or max is given, and is omitted for a note-only axis such as a package name or capacitor type.

param.description: The condition dimension. Recommended vocabulary: T_J, T_A, V_IN, V_OUT, I_OUT, I_LOAD, F, C_OUT, C_IN, ESR, HEADROOM, RIPPLE, BW_LOW, BW_HIGH, V_EN, C_OUT_TYPE, PACKAGE, BOARD. Family-specific axes such as V_GS, V_DS, and F_SW are permitted.

note.description: Free text, for example a capacitor type such as X7R ceramic, or a package name.

allOf.$comment: A unit is required when the axis carries a number.

stimulus.title: Stimulus
stimulus.description: An applied step for a dynamic measurement, for example I_OUT from 0 to 300 mA at 0.2 A/us.

param.description: What is stepped, for example I_OUT or V_IN.

slewUnit.description: Unit of the slew rate, for example A/us or V/us.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: The record of where every value in this document came from. It is what allows a specification to be verified rather than only asserted.

datasheetSha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact datasheet PDF bytes.

sourceUrl.description: Where the datasheet was fetched from.

datasheetRevision.description: Revision string as printed, for example SBVS176K REVISED MARCH 2023.

extractionMethod.description: How the data was produced, for example manual or llm:claude-sonnet-4-5.

confidence.description: Extraction confidence from 0 to 1. Advisory only. It does not by itself imply the data is verified.

verified.description: True only when the data passed a validation suite.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: Base-SI unit symbol. Values are normalized to base units so cross-part numeric comparison is sound. Derived units are included where a datasheet parameter requires them, for example ppm/degC for temperature coefficient and V/us for slew rate. The fractional-rate family ppm, ppm/V, and ppm/A captures dimensionless drift (long-term stability, thermal hysteresis) and the per-volt/per-amp regulation rates that precision references and other parts specify, alongside ppm/degC. A2s is ampere-squared-seconds, the I-squared-t fusing rating a rectifier publishes for fuse coordination. bits is a dimensionless base-2 count (may be fractional): a data converter's resolution and its effective/noise-free resolution and ENOB. A converter's linearity (INL/DNL) and offset/gain error use ppm (of full scale), V, or % rather than the part-relative LSB, so numbers stay comparable across parts; the printed LSB figure is preserved in conditionsVerbatim. Vs is volt-seconds, the time-integral of a voltage transient a DAC publishes as its glitch impulse and digital feedthrough (a printed nV-s is 1e-9 Vs). ppm/degC2 is ppm per degree-Celsius-squared (ppm.K^-2), the second-order (parabolic) temperature coefficient a tuning-fork crystal publishes about its turnover temperature: frequency deviation is the curvature times (T - T_turnover) squared. It is distinct from the linear ppm/degC; the two are not interconvertible. 1 is the dimensionless unit (ISO 80000 uses 1 for a quantity of dimension one): a bare ratio or count that is neither a base-2 count (bits), a voltage-gain ratio (V/V), nor a fraction (%, ppm) - a quartz crystal's quality factor Q and its C0/C1 capacitance ratio are the motivating cases, both pure numbers a datasheet prints as guaranteed spec rows. The photometric and radiometric units serve the LED family: m is the metre (an emitter's peak/dominant/centroid wavelength and spectral bandwidth, printed in nm - 630 nm is 6.3e-7; admitted for optical-length quantities only, never for mechanical package outline); cd is the candela (luminous intensity, an SI base unit; a printed mcd is 1e-3 cd); lm is the lumen (luminous flux, = cd.sr); W/sr is watts per steradian (radiant intensity, the radiometric analogue an IR/UV emitter publishes; a printed mW/sr is 1e-3 W/sr); K is the kelvin used for an absolute colour temperature (a white LED's correlated colour temperature: a 5000 K CCT is a thermodynamic colour point, NOT 5000 degC, so it is distinct from the degC used for ambient/junction temperature); lm/W is luminous efficacy (a guaranteed, binned headline the datasheet prints rather than leaving to be derived); m/degC is a wavelength temperature coefficient (an emitter's peak-wavelength drift, printed in nm/K). Radiant flux stays in W and a colour-rendering index or CIE x/y coordinate stays dimensionless (1). The laser-diode units: W/A is optical watts per amp of drive current, a laser diode's slope (differential) efficiency dP/dI - the slope of its light-versus-current curve (a printed mW/mA is the identical number); m/A is metres per amp, a single-frequency laser's wavelength current-tuning coefficient dLambda/dI (a printed nm/mA is 1e-9 m/A). A laser's linewidth is a frequency width in Hz (a printed MHz/kHz linewidth), its side-mode suppression and relative-intensity-noise stay dB (the RIN's per-Hz reference kept in conditionsVerbatim, like the ADC's dBFS/Hz), and its beam quality M-squared and numerical aperture stay dimensionless (1). The photodiode (photodetector) units invert the emitter's: A/W is amperes per watt, a detector's responsivity (photosensitivity) - the photocurrent it produces per incident optical watt, the literal reciprocal of a laser's W/A slope efficiency (a printed mA/mW is the identical number); W/sqrtHz is watts per root-hertz, the noise equivalent power (NEP) that completes the V/sqrtHz and A/sqrtHz noise-density family; m2 is square metres, a detector's photosensitive/active area (a printed mm2 is 1e-6 m2), a first-class selection parameter distinct from a wavelength or a diameter in m. A detector's avalanche gain, excess-noise factor, and k-factor stay dimensionless (1); its detectivity D* (Jones) is derivable from NEP and area and is not given a unit.
